item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is marginally preferable because its out-of-contract changes are somewhat narrower and its seekable-body handling avoids A’s risky seek-to-end logic. Neither patch is merge-ready against the frozen contract.","reasons":["Both patches violate the required Upload signature by accepting a new upload-option interface instead of `opts ...FilesOption`.","Both incorrectly add association-field APIs, call a new `NewFileWithFields` helper instead of `multipartbody.NewFile`, duplicate `Add` via direct `Raw.Do`, and refactor global retry behavior.","B avoids A’s additional `WithFileFormField` API and does not change `WithFilesQuery`’s return type.","A’s retry helper seeks to EOF to calculate length and assumes a failed seek leaves the offset unchanged; that is not guaranteed and could cause a corrupted first request. B avoids this mutation."],"risks_a":["Changes broader request semantics, ownership, and Content-Length behavior despite the explicit scope restriction.","Upload does not route through `FilesService.Add`, so option and error behavior can drift.","No visible source-reader failure test; association machinery is explicitly prohibited."],"risks_b":["Still has the wrong public signature and substantial prohibited association/retry machinery.","Upload bypasses `FilesService.Add` and does not accept `WithFilesQuery`.","No visible source-reader failure test, and the Upload retry test uses `strings.Reader` rather than an `os.Open`-style streamed source."]}
